case.title: tert-Butyl peroxypivalate synthesis
case.protocol: Aqueous tert-butyl hydroperoxide was converted to potassium tert-butylperoxide with KOH (1.12 equiv), then reacted with pivaloyl chloride in the presence of sodium dodecyl sulfate. The biphasic exothermic reaction was run in a three-necked flask at 23 C for 31 min and afforded tert-butyl peroxypivalate in 53% yield.

proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: From Chemistry Plan: KOH (B) must be added to TBHP (A) first to generate the nucleophile. Then Pivaloyl Chloride (C) is added to the A+B mixture to avoid side reactions between TBHP and Pivaloyl Chloride.
pre_reactor_steps: Mix Stream A (TBHP/SDS/Water) and Stream B (KOH/Water) in a T-mixer to generate potassium tert-butylperoxide in situ.
Mix the A+B effluent with Stream C (Pivaloyl Chloride) in a Y-mixer immediately before the reactor coil.
post_reactor_steps: Quench with Water/Acidic Wash to neutralize excess KOH and hydrolyze unreacted pivaloyl chloride.

Axial dispersion (Pe=36) is significant, suggesting CSTR-like behavior; smaller ID or static mixer could help but 1.0 mm ID is used per calculation. No light source required. BPR not required as T < bp - 20C.
